text:
The headline figure, 72% of customers satisfied, is misleading. The survey was emailed to 40,000 recipients, and 1,000 of them chose to respond. That tells us who was willing to answer, not how satisfied customers are.

Falling response rates make this worse. Pew's telephone response rate dropped from 36% in 1997 to 6% by 2018. Each point of response lost makes the people who do answer more likely to be the delighted or the furious, which skews the sample.

The report quotes a ±3-point margin of error, but that figure assumes random selection, and this data was never randomly selected. The margin covers random sampling error. It does not cover the bias from self-selection.

This lesson is not new. In 1936 the Literary Digest collected 2.4 million returned ballots, far more than any competitor's sample, and confidently picked Landon. Roosevelt carried 46 states.

Analysts should assume the number flatters its sponsor until weighting against census benchmarks shows otherwise.
